function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick‑look guide to the **next big festivals happening in the United States** (as of mid‑2026).  I’ve grouped them by genre so you can pick the one that best matches your interests.  All dates are the *official start dates*—many festivals run for several days, so check the full schedule on the event’s website.

| Festival | Date(s) | Location | What to Expect | Quick Tips |
|----------|---------|----------|----------------|------------|
| **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | **April 1–3, 2026** | Indio, California (Empire Polo Club) | 3‑day outdoor music & art festival featuring top‑tier rock, hip‑hop, indie, and electronic acts.  Art installations, food trucks, and a “Coachella‑style” vibe. | Book tickets early (they sell out fast).  Bring a reusable water bottle (the venue has refill stations). |
| **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | **June 15–18, 2026** | Manchester, Tennessee (Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival Grounds) | 4‑day festival with a mix of rock, folk, hip‑hop, electronic, and world‑music.  Known for its “Bonnaroo” community feel, craft beer, and “Bonnaroo‑style” camping. | Arrive early for the “Bonnaroo‑style” camping experience.  Check the festival’s app for real‑time line‑ups. |
| **Lollapalooza Chicago** | **August 4–7, 2026** | Grant Park, Chicago (Grant Park) | 4‑day festival featuring mainstream pop, rock, hip‑hop, and indie acts.  Food trucks, art installations, and a “Lollapalooza‑style” vibe. | Get a “Lollapalooza‑style” wristband for early entry.  Bring a small backpack (no large bags allowed). |
| **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | **May 27–28, 2026** | French Quarter, New Orleans (Jackson Square) | 2‑day festival celebrating jazz, blues, zydeco, and Cajun music.  Food vendors serve gumbo, jambalaya, and beignets. | Arrive early for the “Jazz‑style” line‑up.  Wear comfortable shoes for walking around the French Quarter. |
| **South by Southwest (SXSW)** | **March 11–20, 2026** | Austin, Texas (Various venues) | 10‑day festival featuring film, music, and interactive media.  Includes panels, concerts, and networking events. | Register for the “SXSW‑style” pass if you want to attend all events.  Book accommodation early—Austin fills up fast. |
| **Burning Man (Black Rock City)** | **August 22–29, 2026** | Black Rock Desert, Nevada | 8‑day event focused on art, self‑expression, and community.  Participants build a temporary city and burn a large wooden effigy. | Prepare for extreme desert conditions (heat, dust).  Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and a “Burning‑Man‑style” survival kit. |
| **Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC) Las Vegas** | **May 12–13, 2026** | Las Vegas Strip (Las Vegas Convention Center) | 2‑day electronic dance music festival with elaborate stages, light shows, and carnival rides. | Buy tickets in advance; they often sell out.  Arrive early for “EDC‑style” security checks. |

---

### How to Find the Next Festival Near You

| Step | Tool / Resource | Why It Helps |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| 1 | **Eventbrite** | Search by city or zip code for local festivals. |
| 2 | **Ticketmaster** | Browse upcoming concerts and festivals. |
| 3 | **Local tourism websites** | Many cities list annual festivals (e.g., NYC’s “NYC Festivals” page). |
| 4 | **Social media hashtags** | #MusicFestival, #FoodFestival, #ArtFestival often reveal upcoming events. |
| 5 | **Google Calendar** | Add “Upcoming US festivals” to your calendar for reminders. |

---

### Quick Checklist Before You Go

| Item | Notes |
|------|-------|
| **Tickets** | Buy through official sites; avoid scalpers. |
| **Accommodation** | Book early—especially for big festivals. |
| **Transportation** | Plan parking or public transit routes. |
| **Weather** | Check forecast; bring appropriate gear. |
| **Health & Safety** | Pack a first‑aid kit, hand sanitizer, and any prescription meds. |
| **Cash & Cards** | Some vendors only accept cash; bring a mix. |

---

#### Want More Details?

If you’d like deeper info on a specific festival (line‑up, ticket tiers, travel tips, etc.), let me know which one and I’ll dig into the specifics for you!
